title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Earlier pages set up the boundary stratification of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification of M_{g,ν}. Strata M_G are indexed by stable dual graphs ("MD-graphes"). A generisation G → G' contracts some edges, i.e. smooths some nodes. For such a pair Grothendieck uses three fundamental groupoids:
- ΠM_G, the fundamental groupoid of the stratum M_G;
- ΠM*_{G,G'}, the fundamental groupoid of the deleted tubular neighbourhood of M_G, intersected with the more generic stratum M_{G'};
- ΠM_{G'}.
They are linked by a specialisation/retraction functor φ_{G,G'}: ΠM*_{G,G'} → ΠM_G and a restriction functor r_{G,G'}: ΠM*_{G,G'} → ΠM_{G'}. Formula (103) on the earlier pages is this diagram. The previous page calls the resulting correspondence the "torseur de générisation" T_{G*,G'}.

This page: transitivity for a composite generisation G → G' → G'' (formula 104).
- Diagram (105) stacks the two correspondences (103) for (G,G') and for (G',G''). Its upper-left corner is ΠM*_{G,G''}, mapping by dashed arrows to ΠM*_{G',G''} and to ΠM*_{G,G'}.
- The square is marked "2 cart". The claim is ΠM*_{G,G''} ≃ ΠM*_{G,G'} ×^{(2)}_{ΠM_{G'}} ΠM*_{G',G''}, a 2-fibre product of groupoids. Note that ΠM_{G'} ≃ Π(M_{G'}, Γ^!_{G',G''}), a fundamental groupoid with a prescribed set of base points.
- Consequences, read from the text:
  1. ΠM*_{G,G''} is an extension of ΠM*_{G,G'} by a twisted free abelian local system Z^{C'}. Here C' is the set of nodes smoothed in G' → G''; this is the fibre of ΠM*_{G',G''} → ΠM_{G'}, generated by Dehn twists about the vanishing cycles.
  2. ΠM*_{G,G'} is itself an extension of ΠM_G by a twisted Z^C.
  3. Hence ΠM*_{G,G''} is an extension of ΠM_G by a twisted Z^{C⊔C'}, itself built from twisted Z^C and Z^{C'}.
- The composite outer diagram (107), ΠM_G ←φ_{G,G''}— ΠM*_{G,G''} —r_{G,G''}→ ΠM_{G''}, is again a generisation correspondence (103) for G → G''. The top arrow r_{G,G''} is the composite r_{G',G''} ∘ (dashed arrow).
- The next page goes on to compare this with the base-point inclusions Γ^!_{G,G'} ⊂ Γ^!_{G,G''} and to state a commutativity (cocycle) property.

Purpose. This builds a coherent system of groupoids and correspondences indexed by the poset of stable graphs under contraction. In effect it is a stratified (exit-path-type) fundamental 2-groupoid of the boundary of M̄_{g,ν}. It serves the 'Teichmüller tower' / structure-at-infinity programme: gluing fundamental groupoids of strata via Dehn-twist extensions.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The 2-cartesian claim is correct here because the DM boundary is a normal-crossings divisor in the stack sense. Locally the deleted neighbourhood of a codim-(|C|+|C'|) stratum is a (C*)^{C⊔C'}-type torsor, which matches the homotopy fibre product. For a general stratified space, composable exit paths need not give such a 2-cartesian square, so the claim uses the normal-crossing structure. Grothendieck does not justify it on this page.

Minor gap: the page says the composite kernel is an extension of twisted Z^C by twisted Z^{C'} without saying it is abelian (direct sum). It is, since Dehn twists about disjoint vanishing cycles commute. This is not checked on the page.
Subscript notation is inconsistent (MD-graph indices dropped, a crossed-out notation change). The roles of C/C' as edge sets versus graph labels must be inferred.

ideas.what: Transitivity of generisation correspondences between fundamental groupoids of boundary strata. The deleted neighbourhood groupoid for G→G'' is the 2-fibre product of those for G→G' and G'→G'' over ΠM_{G'}.
ideas.modern_name: Composition in an exit-path / stratified fundamental 2-category; homotopy links of a normal-crossings stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, unpublished 1990s), Treumann (2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra A.6), Woolf (homotopy links)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and the gluing of fundamental groupoids along the boundary, but not this explicit 2-cartesian transitivity formalism

ideas.what: The fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum is an extension of ΠM_G by a twisted free abelian group Z^{nodes}, generated by Dehn twists.
ideas.modern_name: Dehn-twist extension / inertia at the boundary of M̄_{g,n}; local monodromy of normal-crossing divisors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Bers, Harvey, Deligne–Mumford); profinite versions by Ihara–Nakamura, Boggi
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Iterated extensions: twisted Z^C and twisted Z^{C'} combine to twisted Z^{C⊔C'} along a chain of generisations.
ideas.modern_name: Filtration of boundary inertia along chains of graph contractions

missed.claim: Grothendieck organises the boundary of M̄_{g,ν} as a coherent system of fundamental groupoids of strata. These are linked by correspondences (retraction φ, restriction r), with a 2-cartesian composition law. This is essentially the exit-path / stratified homotopy 2-category of the DM stratification, written before that formalism existed and applied specifically to moduli of curves.
missed.quote: On retrouve (106) dans (105) comme un produit 2-cartésien
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows a stratified-homotopy (exit-path) viewpoint on the Teichmüller tower in Grothendieck's own notes. That viewpoint is relevant to current work on profinite/anabelian structure at infinity of M̄_{g,n}, e.g. Boggi and Hoshi–Mochizuki-type boundary results. Historians crediting exit-path ideas to MacPherson may want to note it. The content itself is fairly standard once formulated.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics, a normal-crossings transitivity of Dehn-twist extensions, is standard to specialists. The notable feature is the systematic 2-categorical exit-path-style organisation of boundary strata groupoids for M_{g,ν} in unpublished notes, which goes beyond what Esquisse spells out.
transcription_corrections: Indices written 'C, C', C''' are, in context and on adjacent pages, the underlined graph labels G, G', G'' (the generisation G → G' → G''). In the exponents Z^{C}, Z^{C'}, Z^{C⊔C'}, the letters probably denote the sets of smoothed nodes/edges.
'un Z^{C'} (torseur)' should likely read 'un Z^{C'} (tordu)', i.e. twisted. Likewise 'Z^C tordu par Z^{C'} tordu' and 'Z^{C⊔C'} tordu'.
'c'est donc une gerbe[?] de nombres cat.' is likely 'c'est donc une extension de groupoïdes/catégories de ΠM*_{G,G'} par un Z^{C'} (tordu)'.
'tors[?] gr[?]cat. de ΠM_C (déjà [?] un[?] une cat. de Z^C torseur par Z^{C'} torseur)' is likely 'vu que [ΠM*_{G,G'}] est une ext. de ΠM_G (dans une ext. de Z^C tordu par Z^{C'} tordu)'.
Circled page number at top is (40).
Top arrow labels: r_{G,G''} over the long arrow and r_{G',G''} on the right arrow; the left vertical arrow is labelled φ_{G,G'}; the square is labelled '(2 cart)'.
Bottom-right annotation: '(≃ Π(M_{G'}, Γ^!_{G',G''}))', with brace labels '(103)' and '(103) pour (G',G'')'.
